source_analysis: Default native service main constructs Usb, registers the default HIDL service and joins its RPC threadpool; constructor initializes singleton state.
setCallback installs a callback and starts a uevent listener; initial query and uevent callbacks enumerate dual_role_usb and report existing status.
Capability queries open mode/data_role/power_role through std::ofstream and close them without role data writes. This is an output-mode open, not a strictly read-only operation.
Only explicit switchRole RPC emits role values. Default startup/query paths contain no gadget configfs, MTP or sys.usb property operations.
Framework UsbPortHidl initial connection registers callback and queries status; pre-systemReady or error callbacks return. Empty port list and initial add/remove handling do not call setPortRoles.
UsbPortManager role switching is in explicit setPortRoles; initial added/removed ports perform status broadcasts, stats and notifications.
Restoring this exact RC reenables class hal startup and interface-based discovery while retaining service executable, class, user and group.
Observed native and Java-stack structure corroborates the published pinned source; whole-ROM source commit identity is not asserted.
limits: This component review does not rehash or modify the full 6.98GB system image; assembly must preserve inode metadata, xattrs, extents and all bytes outside the RC.
Restored HAL permits the wider framework UsbService boot flow to advance, including existing UsbDeviceManager callbacks. Current gadget RC guards must remain preserved.
Explicit later switchRole calls can change USB roles; runtime stability and subsequent hardware failures require observation.
